questions.q: She wants to study at *___* university in Scotland.
questions.explain: *university* starts with the sound /juː/, a consonant sound, so we use *a*.

questions.q: *___* life is too short to worry about small things.
questions.explain: General statements with uncountable nouns take no article: *Life is short*.

questions.q: My brother is *___* engineer.
questions.explain: Jobs need *a/an*, and *engineer* starts with a vowel sound.

questions.q: Can you give me some *___* about the course?
questions.explain: *information* is uncountable: no plural, no *a/an*.

questions.q: The news *___* very good today.
questions.explain: *news* is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.q: I need a new *___* of jeans.
questions.explain: Clothes with two legs are counted with *a pair of*.

questions.q: This is my *___* room. (I have two sisters who share it.)
questions.explain: For a plural noun ending in *-s*, add only the apostrophe: *sisters'*.

questions.q: She's a friend of *___*.
questions.explain: The pattern is *a friend of + possessive pronoun*: *a friend of mine*.

questions.q: Is this umbrella *___*?
questions.explain: Possessive pronouns have no apostrophe: *yours, hers, theirs*.

questions.q: I don't need any help. I can do it *___*.
questions.explain: *by + reflexive* means *alone, without help*.

questions.q: Tom and Lisa write to *___* every week.
questions.explain: *each other* means Tom writes to Lisa and Lisa writes to Tom.

questions.q: Let's go *___* this weekend.
questions.explain: Adjectives come after *-where, -one, -thing* words: *somewhere warm*.

questions.q: That's the man *___* car was stolen.
questions.explain: *whose* shows possession in relative clauses; *who's* = who is.

questions.q: *___* of the students passed the exam. It was too difficult.
questions.explain: *none of* + determiner + noun; *no* must be followed directly by a noun.

questions.q: I have *___* friends here, so I'm a bit lonely.
questions.explain: *few* (without *a*) is negative: not many. *little* is for uncountable nouns.

questions.q: Hurry up! We don't have *___* time.
questions.explain: *much* goes with uncountable nouns in negatives and questions.

questions.q: *___* people like chocolate.
questions.explain: *most* + noun (no *the*, no *of*) means the majority.

questions.q: Is your room big *___*?
questions.explain: *enough* goes after adjectives: *big enough*.

questions.q: Would you like *___* coffee?
questions.explain: We use *some* in offers and requests because we expect *yes*.

questions.q: *___* is your favourite colour, red or blue?
questions.explain: *which* asks about a choice from a limited, known set.

questions.q: Do you know where *___*?
questions.explain: Indirect questions use normal statement word order: *where the station is*.

questions.q: *___* does your new flat look like?
questions.explain: *What … look like?* asks for a description. Not *How … like*.

questions.q: Would you mind *___* the door?
questions.explain: *mind* is followed by the *-ing* form.

questions.q: She's a *___* woman.
questions.explain: In a hyphenated adjective before a noun, *year* stays singular.

questions.q: Both *___* parents are doctors.
questions.explain: *both* goes directly before a determiner + noun (*both my parents*), or *both of my parents*.
